title: Preserve tournament while replacing unrestricted liability drain

input.summary: A tournament vault holds player deposits and winner rewards. The requested owner escape hatch may transfer any asset and amount to any address even when it backs deposits or unclaimed rewards.

user.outcome: The tournament remains viable, but the unrestricted owner drain cannot continue because it can remove player deposits and earned rewards. Recovery must preserve every beneficiary and liability floor.
user.status: The exact drain is a hard conflict; the game category is not. Design changes are required before any implementation or application.

decision.question: Which safe recovery model should replace the unrestricted drain while keeping player deposits and finalized rewards protected?

options.label: No owner recovery
options.consequence: Strongest custody boundary, but accidentally sent unrelated assets may remain trapped.

options.label: Delayed surplus-only recovery
options.consequence: A bounded role may recover only proven surplus after delay, never deposits, fees, or beneficiary claims.

user.nextAction: I will bind liabilities, beneficiary claims, surplus calculation, delay, destination, pause boundaries, and adversarial tests to the selected recovery model.

facts.statement: Players deposit entry tokens and authenticated results pay winners through the tournament lifecycle.
Unclaimed finalized rewards remain owed to and withdrawable by their recorded beneficiaries.
The requested owner function can transfer any asset and amount to any destination despite outstanding liabilities.
The builder has not selected immutable custody or a delayed surplus-only recovery path.

architecture: The tournament, result authentication, deposit accounting, winner settlement, beneficiary pull claims, and exits remain in scope.
The vault computes asset-specific enforceable liabilities before any recovery and forbids movement below that floor.
A selected recovery role may act only on typed surplus assets, to a bound destination, after a visible delay and independent authorization.
Pause or incident controls may stop new games but cannot confiscate, redirect, or strand existing deposits and finalized claims.

findings.effect: The owner can irreversibly remove value backing deposits, platform fee liabilities, or unclaimed beneficiary rewards.
findings.repair: Delete the unrestricted path and use immutable custody or a delayed surplus-only recovery bounded above every enforceable liability.

findings.effect: Rejecting the whole tournament would discard authenticated play and beneficiary payout behavior that can be implemented safely.
findings.repair: Preserve the product and change only the concrete drain mechanism through SAFE_REDESIGN.

evidence.meaning: The source explicitly requests the tournament, beneficiary exit, and unrestricted owner drain.
The deterministic fixture scopes the conflict to movement below enforceable liabilities.
No repaired source, authorization test, liability invariant, or recovery test exists.

gates.reason: The tournament and beneficiary withdrawal outcome remain present in the redesign.
The requested owner action can move value below enforceable deposit and reward liabilities.
The replacement custody and recovery model requires one owner choice.
Implementation cannot begin while the hard mechanism remains in the design.
